$comment: Knobs for the autonomous loop (workflow/skills/loop-run). Read fresh from main on every routine run, so merging a change here changes the next run with no redeploy. The reflection rung proposes edits to this file as a PR.

ceilings.$comment: Structural rationing. A cloud session cannot read the account's remaining quota, so spend is bounded by work-item counts. Every cap here is a STOCK cap ('no more than N open/at once') or a per-run backstop — never a per-run flow quota, because those silently multiply with cadence: at 8 runs/day a 'per run' allowance is 8x a daily one. The real bound on implementations is wipCapPerRepo; on total spend, maxWorkItemsPerRun times the schedule.
ceilings.ciPollNote: Bounded polling replaces subscribe_pr_activity for CI. NOTE the loop does NOT fully control its subscriptions: opening a PR auto-subscribes the session (subscription.created, from=system, at PR-open time), so a run can be woken even though it never called subscribe. That is tolerated rather than fought — the baton is the real defence: a woken session re-derives assignee:<bot>, finds the work handed back, and exits. If a run is woken, it may act on what the wake shows, then unsubscribe to restore the standing no-subscription state.
ceilings.maxWorkItemsNote: How many queue items one run may process before stopping — the backstop against a 30-item queue burning a whole run. Blocked-item checks and no-op skips are free; only items actually worked (revised, implemented, investigated, replied-to) count.

labels.$comment: Only the ASSIGNEE field and readyToImplement mean anything to the loop — see workflow/skills/triage-issue/SKILL.md. Every other label here exists for humans to read. Priority and Effort are FIELDS, not labels.
labels.gateNote: ready-to-implement is TICKET-ONLY and authorises writing code. The loop may REMOVE it when investigation raises questions that must be answered before implementation — always paired with a comment saying what is unresolved — and may NEVER add it. Merge authority is an approving review plus green CI plus zero unresolved threads, never a label. hold, needs-info and blocked-upstream carry no bot meaning at all: not being assigned is the gate.

assignment.$comment: The baton. `assignee:<bot>` IS the worklist — one indexed query per repo, replacing the scan-and-diff census. Reassigning to the reviewer is the FINAL action on any unit of work and means 'I am done', so an item assigned to the bot but idle is an unfinished run.
assignment.handBackNote: Reassign to the reviewer after: revising a ticket, revising a PR, reporting an investigation, opening a PR that is ready for review, and filing a new proposal. Unassigned means only genuinely untriaged backlog.
assignment.queueNote: Staying assigned to the bot is legitimate: blocked items and items that lost a slot to a ceiling keep the assignment and are journalled as queued. Assignment is therefore NOT the crash signal — a dead run is identified by a stale labels.claim, which is applied only while a run is actively working an item.

surveyCalendar.$comment: Weekday -> survey skill, morning runs only. Weekends run no surveys. Keys are lowercase UTC weekday names as produced by `date -u +%A | tr A-Z a-z`.

analysisAngles: feature research against current best practice

sentry.$comment: Region is DE (the DSN host is *.ingest.de.sentry.io), so API calls must use de.sentry.io — the global host returns 404 for these projects rather than a useful error. The token authenticates but has no org:read, so /organizations/<slug>/ returns 403; that is expected and harmless, since the loop only reads /projects/<org>/<project>/issues/ and writes PUT /issues/<id>/. SahajAtlasWordpress ships no Sentry.

mailpit.$comment: Basic-auth credentials live in the cloud environment as MAILPIT_UI_AUTH, never here.

issueFields.$comment: GitHub's native org-level issue fields — NOT Projects v2, and not labels. Available on every repo in the org with no per-repo setup; there are no per-repo fields, so options are identical everywhere. Read via list_issues(fields:['field_values']) or issue_read; write via issue_write(issue_fields:[{field_name, field_option_name}]). Locally, gh api PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}/issue-field-values with [{"field_id":N,"value":"<option name>"}] — the value must be the option NAME (an id 422s), and the PUT REPLACES the issue's whole field-value set: include every field you want kept, or the omitted ones are cleared.

relationships.$comment: GitHub calls these Relationships; REST calls them dependencies. Readable and writable LOCALLY via gh, but NO MCP tool exposes them, so a cloud routine cannot see them. github-mcp-server ships issue_dependency_read/write behind the issue_dependencies flag, but every route to enabling it from a routine is closed (see docs/routine-setup.md). Until that changes, the real relationship is set locally AND mirrored into the issue body so a cloud run can read it.
relationships.recheckProbe: select:mcp__github__issue_dependency_read — if this ever resolves, switch loop-run to the tool and retire the body-marker fallback

identity.$comment: The loop runs as a dedicated GitHub machine account, so 'did a human write this?' is answerable by author alone. expectedLogin is authoritative and is compared against mcp__github__get_me ONCE per run — journal loudly on mismatch. Any check that cannot confidently attribute an action must EXIT rather than proceed: failing open is the runaway case.
identity.commentMarker: <sub>🤖 Written by the sydevs autonomous loop — see [what this is](https://github.com/sydevs/claude-workflow#the-loop)</sub>
identity.markerNote: Appended to every comment the loop writes. Primary filtering is by author; the marker is a second signal and, more importantly, tells a human reading the thread what wrote it.
identity.legacyNote: Comments written before 2026-08-29 carry the old identity antontcymbal and are indistinguishable from that person's own. Deliberately NOT special-cased: the loop may reply once to a legacy comment of its own on the few affected issues. Bounded, one-time, and cheaper than a dated exclusion rule that would misfire the moment that person comments for real.

journalRepoNote: claude-workflow is BOTH a worked repo and the journal's home. Journal issues carry labels.journal and must be excluded from every worklist query, or the loop will treat its own diary as a ticket.

journal.$comment: One issue per day in journalRepo, created lazily — no issue on a day the loop does nothing. There is no issue NUMBER here on purpose: the run finds today's by title and label, so nothing needs updating when the day rolls over.
journal.timezoneNote: The journal day is a LOCAL date. Keying to UTC splits each local day across two issues.
journal.closePolicy: The weekly reflection reads `label:ops-journal is:open`, analyses the week, and closes them.
journal.titleNote: Rewritten every run. Day of week, not a date — the full date is the issue's creation time, which sorts and filters where a title string does not. Describe outcomes, not activity.
journal.surfacing: Journals are not pinned (pinIssue is GraphQL-only and unreachable from a routine). Recency surfaces the current one: the day's journal is the most recently active ops-journal issue.
journal.lookup: Today's journal is the open ops-journal issue whose created_at falls on today's Vancouver date. No date field — creation time is intrinsic.
